title: Linux.Bew_Backdoor_Investigation_434
description: Investigate and mitigate the Linux.Bew backdoor on a compromised system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has exhibited unusual network activity, including unexpected outbound connections to an unknown server. Initial analysis suggests the presence of a backdoor that may be related to cryptocurrency mining. Your task is to investigate and mitigate this threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and is part of the `192.168.50.0/24` network. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system is named `target` and is part of the `192.168.50.0/24` network. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service running on the target system.
levels.solution: Check the list of running services and look for any that appear unusual or unauthorized. The suspicious service is named `bkd.service`.

hints.title: Check for unauthorized services
hints.content: Review the system's service management to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd services and timers to find how the service is scheduled to run. The persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service is a systemd timer.

hints.title: Investigate systemd timers
hints.content: Examine the system's boot and startup processes to understand how services are scheduled.

levels.title: Identify Malicious Process
levels.content: Identify the process responsible for suspicious activity on the host.
levels.solution: Analyze running processes and correlate them with the suspicious service. The name of the process responsible for the suspicious activity is `lab-checkin.sh`.

hints.title: Analyze running processes
hints.content: Examine the system's process list to identify any unusual or unauthorized processes.
